architectureFamilies.name: Locally switchable Bragg coupling
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Permanent momentum structure plus locally increased coupling amplitude or polarization overlap.
architectureFamilies.gate: Requires local Delta n or equivalent coupling near 1e-4-1e-3 over sub-mm to mm lengths while keeping off coupling near 1e-5.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Directly addresses WP-v2-15 by separating kappa_on from kappa_inactive.

architectureFamilies.name: Locally written / induced backward Bragg grating
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Dynamic grating exists only at the active region.
architectureFamilies.gate: Backward Bragg period is about 200 nm; acoustic waves are typically orders of magnitude too coarse, while optical writing has power/persistence issues.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Does not reliably avoid the optical-period momentum problem unless counterpropagating optical writing or a static assist supplies the period.

architectureFamilies.name: Local phase defect / resonant defect
architectureFamilies.mechanism: A mostly detuned or weakly reflective periodic structure is locally converted into a defect resonance.
architectureFamilies.viewingGeometry: Narrowband directional reflection or resonant extraction
architectureFamilies.gate: Promising optical leverage, but moving the defect requires controlled phase or optical-thickness shifts near pi at selected depth.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Could reduce full-grating participation, but addressable defect creation is not yet demonstrated in the bulk geometry.

architectureFamilies.name: Local coupling cancellation / restoration
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Two coupling contributions cancel in the inactive state; local control breaks cancellation.
architectureFamilies.gate: Attractive ON/OFF ratio, but fabrication and phase stability are high risk.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Could produce low inactive coupling without requiring tiny absolute fabrication errors if a robust symmetry mechanism exists.

architectureFamilies.name: Local resonant scattering
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Embedded resonators or resonant planes are shifted into resonance locally.
architectureFamilies.viewingGeometry: Potentially wider-angle scattering or engineered directional output
architectureFamilies.gate: Index shift for high-Q switching is smaller, but high-Q also increases spectral/angular sensitivity and fabrication burden.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Broadens beyond Bragg reflection and may provide better viewing geometry if loss/transparency can be controlled.

architectureFamilies.name: Electro-optic local activation
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Electric field changes index, phase, coupling, polarization, or a resonant condition.
architectureFamilies.viewingGeometry: Depends on structure; usually phase/coupling modulation
architectureFamilies.gate: Fast and mature in guided devices; unresolved risk is localizing strong fields inside a thick volume.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Best dynamic-control family for follow-up because the response is fast and electronically synchronized.

architectureFamilies.name: Acousto-optic local activation
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Acoustic field modulates phase, coupling, resonance, or a defect instead of directly writing the optical-period grating.
architectureFamilies.viewingGeometry: Deflected Bragg output, gated defect, or moving interaction plane
architectureFamilies.gate: Useful for moving envelopes and lower-frequency gating, but direct backward-grating generation remains rejected.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Acoustics should be reconsidered only as a gate for another optical structure.

architectureFamilies.name: Optically controlled / photorefractive activation
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Control light changes local index, carriers, or a holographic grating.
architectureFamilies.viewingGeometry: Can be Bragg-like, phase-like, or absorptive/scattering
architectureFamilies.gate: Fast strong writing tends to require high optical fluence, persistence/erase management, or absorption.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Potentially useful for slow reconfigurable calibration, not the leading display-rate voxel switch.

architectureFamilies.name: Thermo-optic activation
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Temperature changes refractive index or resonance.
architectureFamilies.gate: Required temperature rises for large optical shifts are high, and diffusion destroys fast sub-mm localization.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Good reference mechanism but not a leading display switch.

architectureFamilies.name: Hybrid static momentum + dynamic strong coupling
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Static structure supplies momentum/phase matching; EO/LC/AO/resonant control supplies local ON/OFF interaction.
architectureFamilies.viewingGeometry: Architecture-dependent; can be directional or scattering
architectureFamilies.gate: Most plausible way to avoid optical-period dynamic writing while gaining a large local switching ratio.
architectureFamilies.rationale: This is the strongest architectural direction to model next.

architectureFamilies.name: Thin discrete active planes
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Many transparent addressable planes replace continuous homogeneous depth.
architectureFamilies.viewingGeometry: Plane-wise scattering, Bragg, or resonant output
architectureFamilies.gate: Discrete depth may be visually acceptable and manufacturable, but inactive loss per plane must be extremely low.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Challenges the continuous-depth assumption and gives a practical electronic-addressing route.

architectureFamilies.name: Sparse embedded structures
architectureFamilies.mechanism: Sparse scattering/resonator/grating sheets reduce volume-wide optical burden.
architectureFamilies.gate: Transparency and fabrication uniformity are central risks.
architectureFamilies.rationale: May be a manufacturable compromise between bulk and layered architectures.

architectureFamilies.name: Scanning a thin active layer
architectureFamilies.mechanism: A moving excitation front or boundary creates one thin active optical layer.
architectureFamilies.gate: Can be efficient if the optical interaction is strong; moving-front control and synchronization remain open.
architectureFamilies.rationale: Worth keeping if the active layer is optical/electrical/acoustic, not merely the old strain trough renamed.

feasibilityChecks.requiredChange: Delta n ~= 1.312e-4 for 25% ideal local reflectance
feasibilityChecks.result: Requires about current-scale coupling for 25%, but higher targets require several times current Delta n.

feasibilityChecks.requiredChange: Delta n ~= 1.312e-4 over the active length
feasibilityChecks.result: EO can plausibly tune phase/resonance, but direct full Bragg coupling modulation is field-geometry limited.

feasibilityChecks.requiredChange: Delta n scale 1e-4 to 1e-3 for coupling or resonance tuning
feasibilityChecks.result: Large optical anisotropy is attractive; speed, scattering, alignment, and layered geometry dominate feasibility.

feasibilityChecks.requiredChange: Acoustic period near 200 nm for first-order backward Bragg momentum
feasibilityChecks.demonstratedChange: Typical AOM acoustic wavelength is about 10-100 micrometers
feasibilityChecks.result: REJECT: direct acoustic optical-period grating remains mismatched by tens to hundreds of times even before power/localization.
Ordinary EO index shift is too small for low-Q resonators; high-Q or LC/phase leverage is required.
REJECT for fast bulk voxel switching: temperature rise and diffusion are not compatible with sharp moving depth.

survivingCandidates.name: Hybrid static momentum + electro-optic switchable coupling
survivingCandidates.whyItSurvives: It preserves a permanent phase-matching structure but makes the ON/OFF optical interaction a local electronic material requirement.
survivingCandidates.primaryAdvantage: Fast control and a clear switchable-kappa model target.
survivingCandidates.primaryRisk: Electrode geometry may not localize strong fields through bulk depth without layered construction.
survivingCandidates.nextModel: Implement a switchable-kappa CMT reference with explicit kappa_off, kappa_on, active width, and field-localization assumptions.

survivingCandidates.name: Discrete EO/LC active planes
survivingCandidates.whyItSurvives: It relaxes continuous-depth field localization and trades it for manufacturable plane addressing.
survivingCandidates.primaryAdvantage: Electronic plane selection could be practical while inactive plane loss is directly quantifiable.
survivingCandidates.primaryRisk: Many planes demand very low per-plane haze/loss and may produce discrete depth artifacts.
survivingCandidates.nextModel: Build a layered loss/efficiency model tied to target depth resolution and acceptable inactive transmission.

survivingCandidates.name: Sparse resonant-scatterer or resonator planes
survivingCandidates.whyItSurvives: It can create a stronger localized optical event than weak bulk Bragg reflection and may improve viewing geometry.
survivingCandidates.primaryAdvantage: Resonant scattering gives optical leverage and can be placed only where needed.
survivingCandidates.primaryRisk: Inactive transparency, linewidth control, and material tuning response are unresolved.
survivingCandidates.nextModel: Model Q, filling fraction, inactive detuning, switching shift, and cumulative haze for sparse planes.

survivingCandidates.name: Locally gated phase-defect grating
survivingCandidates.whyItSurvives: It may create a localized resonant state without tuning the entire grating into resonance.
survivingCandidates.primaryAdvantage: Uses coherent resonance for high optical interaction from a compact defect.
survivingCandidates.primaryRisk: Moving or electronically creating the defect may be as hard as the original localization problem.
survivingCandidates.nextModel: Create a transfer-matrix defect-grating reference model only after defining a plausible phase-control mechanism.
